newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-WORLD HURDLES CHAMPION ADKINS ELIMINATED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-WORLD HURDLES CHAMPION ADKINS ELIMINATED.

text.p: Defending champion Derrick Adkins of the United States was eliminated in the semifinals of the men's 400 metres hurdles on Sunday when he faded to fifth after leading for most of the race.
Adkins, 27, dominated the first half of his semifinal, but wilted over the last 50 metres and appeared to be standing still as the other runners overtook him in the final few strides.
Russian Ruslan Mashchenko won in 48.54 seconds despite clattering the final barrier, followed by Jamaican Dinsdale Morgan (48.56) who took the second automatic qualifying place to the final.
Adkins, one of the top 400 hurdlers in the world over the past few years said: "I just ran out of gas, I don't know what happened, I just didn't have any energy left and I don't know why."
American Bryan Bronson was the fastest qualifer for Monday's final after winning his semifinal in a time of 47.83 seconds, a time only he has bettered this year.
Samuel Matete of Zambia, the 1991 world champion, qualified as one of the fastest losers.
